intro: Austin rewards visitors with music, food, and outdoorsy fun. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; a single commuter rail line (Red Line) runs north-south.
Capital Metro buses cover downtown, the Capitol, and South Congress; fares are about $1.25 one way.
Ride apps Uber and Lyft work well; taxis are available but less common.
Driving is common but traffic is heavy at rush hour; I-35 is often jammed.
Downtown and UT are walkable; summers are very hot.
Bikes are popular; bike lanes exist on most major streets.

ut_austin.name: University of Texas at Austin
ut_austin.hours: Campus grounds open daily; buildings vary — check on the day
ut_austin.tip: Walk the South Mall to the Main Building tower. The Blanton Museum and LBJ Library sit at the edges of campus.

sxsw.name: SXSW (South by Southwest)
sxsw.price_text: Badges and wristbands only; prices vary by year — check on the day
sxsw.hours: Runs about a week in March; venues set their own hours
sxsw.tip: Book badges and hotels months ahead. Many free and side events run alongside the official programme.

cotaland.name: COTALAND
cotaland.price_text: Ticketed; check current prices on the day
cotaland.hours: Seasonal hours — check on the day
cotaland.tip: It sits next to Circuit of the Americas, far from downtown. Plan a car or rideshare and check race-weekend crowds.

parks_n_pizza.name: Austin's Park N Pizza
parks_n_pizza.price_text: All-day wristbands and single rides; check on the day
parks_n_pizza.hours: Usually open daily, longer on weekends — check on the day
parks_n_pizza.tip: Good for families with kids. Go early on weekends to beat the lines.

tom_foolerys.name: Tom Foolerys Adventure Park, Texas
tom_foolerys.price_text: Pay per attraction or by wristband; check on the day
tom_foolerys.hours: Indoor park hours vary — check on the day
tom_foolerys.tip: An indoor option for rainy or very hot days. Confirm hours before you drive out.

frida_portrait.name: Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird
frida_portrait.landmark: Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird
frida_portrait.price_text: Included with museum admission; check on the day
frida_portrait.hours: Tue–Sun, closed Monday — check on the day
frida_portrait.tip: The Frida Kahlo painting hangs at the Harry Ransom Center on the UT campus. Check it is on display before you go.

franklin_bbq.name: Franklin Barbecue
franklin_bbq.price_text: ≈ USD 15–30 per person; sold by weight
franklin_bbq.hours: Tue–Sun until sold out; closed Monday
franklin_bbq.tip: Arrive before opening and expect a long line. It often sells out by early afternoon.

south_congress.name: South Congress Avenue walk
south_congress.hours: Shops and cafes set their own hours
south_congress.tip: Walk north toward the Capitol for the classic view. Best in the late afternoon when the shops are open.

congress_bridge.name: Congress Avenue Bridge bats
congress_bridge.tip: Stand on the bridge or the grassy bank below. Bats fly out around dusk in warm months.

state_capitol.name: Texas State Capitol
state_capitol.hours: Weekdays and weekends; check on the day
state_capitol.tip: The grounds and rotunda are free. Go early to avoid the heat and tour groups.

zilker_park.name: Zilker Park and Barton Springs
zilker_park.price_text: Park free; Barton Springs Pool has an entry fee — check on the day
zilker_park.hours: Park open daily; pool hours vary by season
zilker_park.tip: The spring-fed pool is cool year-round. Bring a towel and check pool hours before you go.

rainey_street.name: Rainey Street bars
rainey_street.hours: Bars open afternoon into late night
rainey_street.tip: Old houses turned into bars. Busiest on weekend evenings; go earlier for a calmer drink.

sixth_street.name: Sixth Street entertainment district
sixth_street.price_text: Free to walk; pay per venue
sixth_street.hours: Livelier at night; some venues close late
sixth_street.tip: Loud and busy on weekend nights. Keep an eye on your belongings and plan a rideshare home.

east_austin_food.name: East Austin food and coffee walk
east_austin_food.hours: Cafes and restaurants set their own hours
east_austin_food.tip: Wander between small cafes, taco spots and bakeries. Many places close early in the week.

lady_bird_lake.name: Lady Bird Lake hike-and-bike trail
lady_bird_lake.tip: A flat loop along the water. Rent a kayak or walk a short stretch at sunset.

blanton.name: Blanton Museum of Art
blanton.price_text: Ticketed; free on some days — check on the day
blanton.tip: Strong collection of American and Latin American art. Check for free-admission days before you go.

torchys.name: Torchy's Tacos
torchys.hours: Open daily, usually late — check on the day
torchys.tip: A local taco chain with several branches. Good budget stop on South Congress.

mount_bonnell.name: Mount Bonnell viewpoint
mount_bonnell.tip: Short stair climb to a view over the lake and hills. Go at sunset but bring water in summer.

bat_cruise.name: Lady Bird Lake boat cruise
bat_cruise.price_text: ≈ USD 20–40 per person; check on the day
bat_cruise.tip: A relaxed way to see the skyline and the bat bridge from the water. Book ahead on weekends.

bullock_museum.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
bullock_museum.hours: Open daily; check on the day
bullock_museum.tip: Good for Texas history and a big-screen film. A solid indoor break from the heat.

rainbow_cattle.name: Rainbow Cattle Company
rainbow_cattle.tip: A long-running South Congress bar. Casual stop after a walk down the avenue.

plans.for: One full day of Austin history and art, from the Capitol to the bats at sunset.

stays.why: Walk to the Capitol, Congress Avenue and Rainey Street. Best base for a first visit and nightlife.
Shops, cafés and food trucks on SoCo; a short ride or walk over the bridge to downtown.
Cheaper rooms near campus and the Blanton Museum; walkable and bus-friendly.
Galleries, bars and some of the city's best food; close to downtown but quieter.

food: Try Texas BBQ brisket and ribs. Popular spots have long lines; go early or expect a wait.
Breakfast tacos are a local staple. Cheap, filling and sold at many taquerias and trucks.
Food trucks cluster on South Congress and in East Austin. Cash is handy at some.
Book ahead for dinner on weekends, especially downtown and East Austin.
Tap water is safe to drink. Many places refill bottles; summers are hot, so carry water.
more_time: Add a day trip to the Hill Country: small towns and swimming holes west of the city. A car helps.
Swap an afternoon for a lake day on Lake Austin or Lady Bird Lake: kayak or paddleboard rentals.
Music fans can add a night of live shows on Sixth Street or Red River; check listings on the day.
